title: A resumed cut reads the cancelled CI run its earlier attempt left on the candidate, and stops red on it
body:
ci-state's verdict over the candidate (lib/cmd/ci-state, cistate_verdict_on, cistate_rows and cistate_rank) lists every run of the workflow at the release commit on the candidate's ref, through release_runs_list, and takes the worst of them: failed over pending over green. Nothing bounds that list to the runs this attempt's push started.

A cut that stops after its candidate push deletes the candidate branch, and GitHub cancels the run it started. A resume pushes the candidate again, and that starts a fresh run at the same sha on the same ref. The verdict then reads both: the old run's `cancelled` ranks as failed, the candidate leg reads red, and the resume stops and deletes the candidate again, cancelling the fresh run too. So every resume after a stopped cut inherits its predecessor's cancelled run, and none can go green.

Seen in a consumer's patch cut, 2026-11-10: the first attempt stopped at its macOS stage, which could not read the notary keychain from the shell that ran it, and its candidate run was cancelled. hv's resume 9 minutes later pushed the candidate again (a fresh run in progress) and read the old run as cancelled 39 seconds later, then stopped.

Expected: the candidate leg decides on the runs of this attempt alone, those created at or after its own candidate push, or the run that push started, and names any older run at the sha as passed over rather than ranking it.

Workaround until then: delete each cancelled run at the sha (`gh run delete <id>`, a GitHub write) before resuming.

## Resolution

Fixed in one landing on main, c3194c08d23cf862556447d7aa436ee797fdf7be (2026-11-11 07:11Z), unit 0330-1 from the tested tip ef5fa529, landed in devbin 0.1.22's stack after 0332-1; unpushed until devbin's next cut, proved on its own arms under hv's rule of 2026-11-05 (red at the base's code, green at the fix) in one slot on devbin-vc's desk. It takes the shape the issue expected, by run id: the candidate leg decides on its own push's runs, and names each older run at the sha as passed over.

- ci-state --runs <sha> prints the ids of the workflow's runs at <sha> on the ref DEVBIN_RELEASE_TAG names, one a line, through release_runs_list, and exits 1 naming why when it cannot list them whole: no ref, a repository it cannot name, no gh, or a list as long as its limit.
- The cut's candidate start, with the built-in query, reads them once before its push, in one bounded ask, and says on stderr which runs it found. Every later read of the leg hands them to the query as DEVBIN_RELEASE_PASSED_OVER. A list it cannot read is said, and none is passed over, as before.
- ci-state's verdict, with a ref, passes over the runs DEVBIN_RELEASE_PASSED_OVER names and names each after its detail, "passed over run <id> (<conclusion>), from before this push". With only such runs it is none, and a value that is not run ids is unknown.
- Ids, not a time bound, since a bound on a run's creation would compare the cut's clock with GitHub's. A run GitHub had not yet listed when --runs read is still ranked, and a resume minutes later never meets one.
- A project's own query is handed no such list and keeps LEG_CAND_BEFORE. The cut unsets an inherited DEVBIN_RELEASE_PASSED_OVER at its start, as it does DEVBIN_RELEASE_TAG. A dry run and release status push nothing and rank every run as before.
- docs/configuration.md and lib/pages/release.md say so, and lib/pages/ci-state.md gives --runs and the passed-over runs.

Five new arms: four in ci-state.bats (a passed-over cancelled run beside this push's run gives pending and then green, each naming it; passed-over runs alone give none; a value that is not run ids is unknown; --runs lists the ids on the ref and fails naming gh's words or the missing ref) and one in releasecut.bats, the incident: a cut stopped at its legs is run again, its earlier attempt's run 42 cancelled at the release commit on the candidate's branch and this push's run 43 green, and it names 42 as passed over and tags on 43. All five were red at the base, each on its own finding: the base ranks the passed-over cancelled run as the verdict, failed, reads DEVBIN_RELEASE_PASSED_OVER nowhere and has no --runs, and its resumed cut held its candidate pending to ci.wait on run 42 though run 43 was green. Five green legs, 60 arms, were green at the fix: ci-state.bats whole, the new cut arm, the two arms of a cut run again after a red candidate, and the arm over the built-in query's --fires. bin/devbin check lint at the fix was clean. The workaround, deleting each cancelled run at the sha before a resume, is no longer needed.
